es: Identificar atenuadores (it seems, a bit, slightly, might, I wonder if, I'd suggest) en una consulta médica y entender qué mensaje real esconden.

vocabulary.es: decir con todas las letras, explicitar

teaching.en: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly higher than we would like, although the other results are perfectly normal.
teaching.es: Parece que tu presión arterial es algo más alta de lo que querríamos, aunque el resto de los resultados son perfectamente normales.
teaching.explanationEs: It seems that y slightly suavizan la noticia: el mensaje real es «tienes la tensión alta».
segments: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly higher than
we would like, although the other results are perfectly normal.
teaching.audioText: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly higher than we would like, although the other results are perfectly normal.

teaching.en: Doctors often break the news in stages and downplay it with phrases such as a bit worrying, so a patient must learn to read between the lines.
teaching.es: Los médicos suelen dar la noticia por etapas y restarle importancia con frases como a bit worrying, así que el paciente debe aprender a leer entre líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Break the news = comunicar algo difícil; downplay = restar importancia; read between the lines = entender lo no dicho.
segments: Doctors often break the news in stages and downplay it with phrases such as
a bit worrying, so a patient must learn to read between the lines.
teaching.audioText: Doctors often break the news in stages and downplay it with phrases such as a bit worrying, so a patient must learn to read between the lines.

teaching.en: I wonder if we could try a different medicine is not really a question; it is a polite way of telling the patient what the doctor plans to do.
teaching.es: I wonder if we could try a different medicine no es realmente una pregunta: es una forma cortés de decir al paciente lo que el médico piensa hacer.
teaching.explanationEs: I wonder if + could: parece una duda, pero el médico suele proponer un cambio.
segments: I wonder if we could try a different medicine is not really a question; it
is a polite way of telling the patient what the doctor plans to do.
teaching.audioText: I wonder if we could try a different medicine is not really a question; it is a polite way of telling the patient what the doctor plans to do.

teaching.en: When a doctor says I'd suggest you rest for a week, she will not spell out that it is an order, but she is giving an instruction in a gentle voice.
teaching.es: Cuando una doctora dice I'd suggest you rest for a week, no te dirá con todas las letras que es una orden, pero da una instrucción con voz suave.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd suggest suena amable, pero el médico espera que lo hagas; spell out = decir explícitamente.
segments: When a doctor says I'd suggest you rest for a week, she will not spell out
that it is an order, but she is giving an instruction in a gentle voice.
teaching.audioText: When a doctor says I'd suggest you rest for a week, she will not spell out that it is an order, but she is giving an instruction in a gentle voice.

teaching.en: You should hedge carefully in a report: might, it seems and a little let you describe uncertain results without sounding careless.
teaching.es: Debes atenuar con cuidado en un informe: might, it seems y a little permiten describir resultados inciertos sin parecer descuidado.
teaching.explanationEs: Hedge = protegerse con matices; los atenuadores expresan el grado de certeza real.
segments: You should hedge carefully in a report: might, it seems and
a little let you describe uncertain results without sounding careless.
teaching.audioText: You should hedge carefully in a report: might, it seems and a little let you describe uncertain results without sounding careless.

teaching.en: The patient might need another test next week: in a consultation, might is often a polite way of saying that the test is needed.
teaching.es: Puede que el paciente necesite otra prueba la semana próxima: en una consulta, might suele ser una forma cortés de decir que la prueba es necesaria.
teaching.explanationEs: Might suaviza: en una consulta suele significar que hay que hacerla.
segments: The patient might need another test next week: in a consultation, might
is often a polite way of saying that the test is needed.
teaching.audioText: The patient might need another test next week: in a consultation, might is often a polite way of saying that the test is needed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje real esconde la frase de la doctora?

choices.text: There is a real problem, but it can be treated.
The doctor is unsure whether the results are correct.
There is a minor problem that will disappear without any treatment.

feedback.es: Quitados los atenuadores, queda una noticia real (hay un problema) junto con una promesa de tratamiento.

hint.es: Quita it seems y small: ¿qué noticia queda?

origin.text: Doctor: “It seems there is a small problem with your results, but nothing we cannot manage together.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Me pregunto si podríamos hacer otro análisis de sangre el viernes.»

feedback.es: I wonder if + could es la fórmula indirecta con la que el médico propone una prueba que quiere hacer.

origin.text: The results are not clear yet. I ___ if we could do another blood test on Friday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Parece que tu presión arterial está un poco alta.»

answer.text: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly high

feedback.es: It seems that abre la noticia y slightly rebaja el adjetivo high sin ocultar el problema.

hint.es: Empieza con it seems that y termina con el adjetivo.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada atenuador con el mensaje real del médico.

pairs: I wonder if you could wait.

feedback.es: Cada atenuador rebaja el tono, pero el mensaje real sigue: un valor alto, una preocupación, una orden o una petición.

pairs: I wonder if you could wait.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la hija insistió en acompañar a su padre.

choices.text: She wanted to make sure her father would drink less coffee.
She realised the doctor was more worried than her words suggested.
She suspected that the doctor did not trust her father's answers.

feedback.es: La hija leyó entre líneas: tanta suavización indicaba que la preocupación era mayor de lo que decían las palabras.

origin.audio: After the tests, Dr Sara sat down with Mr Lopez and said: It seems your blood pressure is slightly high, and the results are a bit worrying, to be honest. I'd suggest you drink less coffee, and I wonder if you could come back on Friday for another test. Mr Lopez smiled with relief, thinking it was nothing. His daughter, who had read between the lines, noticed that the doctor had softened every single sentence, and she insisted on coming with him.

prompt.es: Completa: «La doctora optó por restar importancia a la noticia.»

feedback.es: Downplay describe rebajar la importancia de algo: la doctora no miente, pero lo presenta como menos grave.

origin.text: The doctor did not want to alarm him, so she chose to ___ the news by saying that the results were only a bit worrying.

prompt.es: ¿Qué espera realmente la doctora de la paciente?

choices.text: That she waits a month without doing anything different.
That she feels safe and forgets about the matter.
That she changes her food and books a visit soon.

feedback.es: Tras «might be a good idea» y «I wonder whether» hay dos instrucciones reales: comer menos azúcar y volver pronto.

origin.text: Doctor: “It might be a good idea to eat less sugar, and I wonder whether we could arrange another visit next month. There is no need to worry, but let's not leave it too long.”

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender el médico con su última frase?

choices.text: That the matter needs attention, but there is no reason to panic.
That the matter is probably minor, so the test is just to be safe.
That the matter is probably serious, so he should prepare for bad news.

feedback.es: La doble negación equilibra tranquilidad y aviso: no hay que asustarse, pero tampoco ignorar el problema.

origin.audio: Good morning, Mr Reed. The results are slightly unusual, and there may be something we need to look at more closely. I'd suggest another test on Monday to be sure. I wouldn't want you to worry before we know more, but I also wouldn't want you to ignore this.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te aconsejaría que descansaras unos días, aunque decides tú.»

feedback.es: I'd suggest that… es una recomendación amable que, en boca de un médico, equivale a una instrucción.

origin.text: I'd ___ that you rest for a few days, although of course the decision is yours. It might help your results.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Puede que el paciente necesite una segunda prueba.»

answer.text: The patient might need a second test

feedback.es: Might + verbo base suaviza la necesidad: en una consulta suele significar que conviene hacerla.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pide realmente el paciente con la última frase de su carta?

choices.text: That the doctor cancels the second test he has suggested.
That the doctor stops softening the news and speaks clearly.
That the doctor sends him the results of the first test.

feedback.es: El paciente ha leído los atenuadores y pide un mensaje claro: quiere saber si debe preocuparse de verdad.

origin.text: Dear Dr Lane, thank you for your message. I understand that the results are slightly unusual and that you would suggest another test. I would be grateful if you could tell me clearly whether I should be worried.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el mensaje real del médico.

choices.text: The result is bad, and there is nothing more to be done.
The result is fine, and the medicine is only to be safe.
The result is bad, treatment is needed, and it can be managed.

feedback.es: No the best y I'm afraid anuncian mala noticia; la oferta del lunes y «we can manage» indican que hay tratamiento.

origin.audio: To be honest, the result is not the best, and I'm afraid we need to start the medicine soon. I wonder if you could come in on Monday, so that we can explain how to take it. It is important, but it is something we can manage.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su presión parece estar algo baja, así que la enfermera la revisará otra vez.»

feedback.es: Seems to be + adjetivo presenta la noticia con distancia y es un atenuador típico de la consulta.

origin.text: Her blood pressure ___ to be slightly low, so the nurse will check it again in an hour.
